```{r setup}
# ---- Setup ----
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(purrr)

sims <- 0:999

alpha_main  <- 0.05
alpha_first <- 0.05

figures_dir <- "Z:/Projects/EMA_Project/Scripts/Figures"

point_size  <- 3
point_alpha <- 0.3
first_point_size  <- 2   
first_point_alpha <- 0.125

# ---- Studies ----
studies <- list(
  random = list(
    label     = "Simulation2 (Random STMs)",
    fig_title = "Simulation: Random State Transition Matrices",
    base_dir  = "Z:/Projects/EMA_Project/Scripts/Output/Simulation2_Results",
    prefix    = "SIM2",
    families  = c(
      "Null"      = "Sim_result_y_null_X_sim_%d.csv",
      "Linear"    = "Sim_result_y_poly1_X_sim_%d.csv",
      "Quadratic" = "Sim_result_y_poly2_X_sim_%d.csv"
    )
  ),
  real = list(
    label     = "Simulation (Real STMs)",
    fig_title = "Simulation: Real State Transition Matrices",
    base_dir  = "Z:/Projects/EMA_Project/Scripts/Output/Simulation_Results",
    prefix    = "SIM",
    families  = c(
      "Null"      = "Sim_result_y_null_RP_sim_%d.csv",
      "Linear"    = "Sim_result_y_poly1_RP_sim_%d.csv",
      "Quadratic" = "Sim_result_y_poly2_RP_sim_%d.csv"
    )
  )
)

# Panel titles within each 3-panel figure
panel_titles <- c(
  "Null"      = "Null",
  "Linear"    = "Linear",
  "Quadratic" = "Quadratic"
)

needed_cols <- c("Specification", "Parameter", "Std_Err", "Observations",
                 "FirstOrder_Param", "FirstOrder_StdErr", "FirstOrder_Obs")

# ---- Helpers: reading & significance ----

# Standardize/rename common column variants to canonical names
standardize_cols <- function(df) {
  rename_map <- c(
    "Std.Err"              = "Std_Err",
    "SE"                   = "Std_Err",
    "N"                    = "Observations",
    "FirstOrder.Parameter" = "FirstOrder_Param",
    "FirstOrderParam"      = "FirstOrder_Param",
    "FirstOrder.StdErr"    = "FirstOrder_StdErr",
    "FO_StdErr"            = "FirstOrder_StdErr",
    "FirstOrder.Obs"       = "FirstOrder_Obs",
    "FO_Obs"               = "FirstOrder_Obs",
    "Spec"                 = "Specification",
    "P.val"                = "P_value"
  )
  # only rename variants that exist and whose canonical name isn't already present
  old <- intersect(names(df), names(rename_map))
  old <- old[!rename_map[old] %in% names(df)]
  if (length(old)) {
    df <- dplyr::rename(df, !!!setNames(old, rename_map[old]))  # new_name = old_name
  }
  df
}

# CI significance at a fixed alpha
compute_ci_sig <- function(beta, se, alpha) {
  ok    <- is.finite(beta) & is.finite(se) & se > 0
  z     <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
  lower <- beta - z * se
  upper <- beta + z * se
  sig   <- ok & ((lower > 0) | (upper < 0))
  tibble(sig = sig, lower = lower, upper = upper)
}

# Read a whole family (pattern) across sims into one combined DF
read_family <- function(base_dir, pattern) {
  files <- file.path(base_dir, sprintf(pattern, sims))
  exists_mask <- file.exists(files)

  if (!any(exists_mask)) stop("No matching files found for pattern: ", pattern)
  if (any(!exists_mask)) {
    message("Skipping missing files for pattern ", pattern, ": ",
            paste(sims[!exists_mask], collapse = ", "))
  }

  read_one <- function(fp, sim_id) {
    df <- suppressMessages(read_csv(fp, show_col_types = FALSE))
    df$sim <- sim_id
    standardize_cols(df)
  }

  purrr::map2_dfr(files[exists_mask], sims[exists_mask], read_one)
}

# Keep complete rows and add significance flags for both models
prepare_family <- function(df, fam) {
  missing_cols <- setdiff(needed_cols, names(df))
  if (length(missing_cols)) {
    stop("Missing columns for ", fam, ": ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }

  df <- df %>% filter(if_all(all_of(needed_cols), ~ !is.na(.x)))

  ci_main  <- compute_ci_sig(df$Parameter,        df$Std_Err,           alpha_main)
  ci_first <- compute_ci_sig(df$FirstOrder_Param, df$FirstOrder_StdErr, alpha_first)

  df %>%
    mutate(
      sig_main  = ci_main$sig,  lower_main  = ci_main$lower,  upper_main  = ci_main$upper,
      sig_first = ci_first$sig, lower_first = ci_first$lower, upper_first = ci_first$upper
    )
}

# ---- Helpers: plotting (multiverse-figure style) ----

spec_levels <- c("Proportion", "Pearson", "Spearman", "Euclid", "Pairwise")

spec_colors <- c(
  "Proportion" = "steelblue",
  "Pearson"    = "seagreen",
  "Spearman"   = "seagreen",
  "Euclid"     = "seagreen",
  "Pairwise"   = "darkgoldenrod"
)

parse_specification <- function(spec_vec) {
  tibble(
    Proportion = as.integer(str_detect(spec_vec, "Proportion")),
    Pearson    = as.integer(str_detect(spec_vec, "Pearson")),
    Spearman   = as.integer(str_detect(spec_vec, "Spearman")),
    Euclid     = as.integer(str_detect(spec_vec, "Euclid")),
    Pairwise   = as.integer(str_detect(spec_vec, "Pairwise"))
  )
}

# Second-order (circles) and first-order (triangles) coefficients, both ordered by the
# second-order estimate. Colour = each model's own CI: green = excludes 0, tomato = includes 0.
create_coefficient_plot <- function(df_sorted, title, tag, ylims) {
  ggplot(df_sorted, aes(x = Index)) +
    geom_point(aes(y = FirstOrder_Param, color = Color_First, shape = "First-Order"),
               size = first_point_size, alpha = first_point_alpha) +
    geom_point(aes(y = Parameter, color = Color, shape = "Second-Order"),
               size = point_size, alpha = point_alpha) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 2) +
    scale_color_identity() +
    scale_shape_manual(
      name   = NULL,
      values = c("Second-Order" = 16, "First-Order" = 17),
      breaks = c("Second-Order", "First-Order"),
      guide  = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 10, alpha = 1, color = "grey30"))
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = ylims) +
    labs(title = title, x = "", y = "Beta Coefficient") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 6) +
    theme(
      plot.title   = element_text(size = 44, hjust = 0.2, face = "bold"),
      plot.tag     = element_text(size = 54, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 34, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 34, face = "bold"),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 34, face = "bold"),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 1),
      legend.text  = element_text(size = 34, face = "bold"),
      plot.margin = margin(t = 5.5, r = 40, b = 5.5, l = 5.5)
    )
}

create_specification_plot <- function(df_sorted) {
  long_data <- parse_specification(df_sorted$Specification) %>%
    mutate(Index = df_sorted$Index) %>%
    pivot_longer(-Index, names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value") %>%
    mutate(
      Variable = factor(Variable, levels = spec_levels),
      Fill     = ifelse(Value == 1L, as.character(Variable), NA_character_)
    )

  ggplot(long_data, aes(x = Index, y = Variable, fill = Fill)) +
    geom_tile(height = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = spec_colors, na.value = "white", guide = "none") +
    labs(x = "Specification", y = "Analytic Dimension") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 30, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 30, face = "bold"),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 34, face = "bold"),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 34, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position  = "none",
      plot.margin = margin(t = 5.5, r = 40, b = 5.5, l = 5.5)
    )
}

# One panel = coefficient plot stacked on spec heatmap
make_panel <- function(df, title, tag, ylims) {
  df_sorted <- df %>%
    arrange(Parameter) %>%
    mutate(
      Index       = row_number(),
      Color       = ifelse(sig_main,  "green3", "tomato"),
      Color_First = ifelse(sig_first, "green3", "tomato")
    )
  create_coefficient_plot(df_sorted, title, tag, ylims) /
    create_specification_plot(df_sorted) +
    plot_layout(heights = c(2, 1))
}

# One figure per study = Null | Linear | Quadratic, tagged a/b/c,
# sharing one y-range: the min and max across all three panels (both models)
make_study_figure <- function(fam_list, fig_title) {
  all_y <- unlist(map(fam_list, ~ c(.x$Parameter, .x$FirstOrder_Param)))
  ylims <- range(all_y[is.finite(all_y)])

  tags   <- letters[seq_along(fam_list)]
  panels <- map2(seq_along(fam_list), names(fam_list),
                 ~ make_panel(fam_list[[.x]], panel_titles[[.y]], tags[.x], ylims))

  wrap_plots(panels, ncol = 3) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(
      title = fig_title,
      theme = theme(
        plot.title      = element_text(size = 54, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "bottom"
      )
    ) &
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

# ---- Helpers: summaries ----

# Null: false positive rates for BOTH first- and second-order models
summarise_null <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    summarise(
      N_estimates   = n(),
      Mean_N_Second = mean(Observations),
      FPR_First     = 100 * mean(sig_first),
      FPR_Second    = 100 * mean(sig_main),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

# Linear: power for BOTH first- and second-order models (both correctly specified)
summarise_linear <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    summarise(
      N_estimates   = n(),
      Mean_N_First  = mean(FirstOrder_Obs),
      Mean_N_Second = mean(Observations),
      Power_First   = 100 * mean(sig_first),
      Power_Second  = 100 * mean(sig_main),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

# Quadratic: detection for the SECOND-order model only
# (first-order is misspecified for a quadratic truth, so it is not evaluated)
summarise_power <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    summarise(
      N_estimates   = n(),
      Mean_N_Second = mean(Observations),
      Power_Second  = 100 * mean(sig_main),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
```

```{r load-data}
# Read every family once; everything below uses study_data
study_data <- list()

for (s in names(studies)) {
  st <- studies[[s]]
  for (fam in names(st$families)) {
    message("Processing: ", st$label, " / ", fam)
    study_data[[st$label]][[fam]] <-
      read_family(st$base_dir, st$families[[fam]]) %>%
      prepare_family(fam)
  }
}
```

# Figures

```{r study-figures, fig.width = 32, fig.height = 20}
for (s in names(studies)) {
  st <- studies[[s]]
  p <- make_study_figure(study_data[[st$label]], st$fig_title)
  print(p)
  ggsave(
    filename  = file.path(figures_dir, paste0(st$prefix, "_multiverse_panels.png")),
    plot      = p,
    width     = 32,
    height    = 20,
    dpi       = 300,
    limitsize = FALSE
  )
}
```

# Tables: both studies

## Percent significant (all families, both models)

```{r overall-summary}
imap_dfr(study_data, function(fams, study) {
  imap_dfr(fams, function(df, fam) {
    tibble(
      Study  = study,
      Family = fam,
      Series = c("Second-Order", "First-Order"),
      Percent_Significant = 100 * c(mean(df$sig_main), mean(df$sig_first))
    )
  })
}) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

```{r table-data}
null_data   <- bind_rows(map(study_data, "Null"),      .id = "Study")
linear_data <- bind_rows(map(study_data, "Linear"),    .id = "Study")
quad_data   <- bind_rows(map(study_data, "Quadratic"), .id = "Study")
```

## Null: false positive rate (all specifications pooled)

Under the null, these percentages are false positive rates. Nominal is 5%.

```{r null-overall}
null_data %>%
  group_by(Study) %>%
  summarise_null() %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## Null: false positive rate by specification

```{r null-by-spec}
null_data %>%
  group_by(Study, Specification) %>%
  summarise_null() %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## Linear: first- vs second-order power (all specifications pooled)

Both models are correctly specified for a linear truth, so a significant estimate counts as a correct detection for each. Not broken down by specification.

```{r linear-overall}
linear_data %>%
  group_by(Study) %>%
  summarise_linear() %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

## Quadratic: second-order detection and false negative rate (all specifications pooled)

A significant second-order estimate counts as a correct detection, since the true effect is nonzero; a non-significant one is a false negative. First-order results are intentionally excluded because that model is misspecified for a quadratic relationship.

```{r quad-overall}
quad_data %>%
  group_by(Study) %>%
  summarise_power() %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## Quadratic: second-order detection and false negative rate by specification

```{r quad-by-spec}
quad_data %>%
  group_by(Study, Specification) %>%
  summarise_power() %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```
